newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'shita Elec April-June parent sales up 7-8% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: M'shita Elec April-June parent sales up 7-8% yr/yr.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd's parent sales for the April-June period rose seven to eight percent year-on-year, company president Yoichi Morishita told a news conference on Thursday.
Morishita also said that the company's parent and group earnings in the first half of the current business year would likely be as expected.
"Business in April-June moved as we planned thanks to robust exports, despite weak sales of air-conditioners, televisions and refrigerators in June," he said.
He also said Matsushita would set up a product development base in Silicon Valley in the United States by January.
The company said in a statement that it would establish the West Coast Product Development Center of Panasonic Technologies Inc in Silicon Valley on January 1, 1998.
Panasonic Technologies is a wholly owned U.S. subsidiary of Matsushita Electric Industrial.
The new product development facility is expected to have 70 staff by 2000.
Matsushita said the new facility would pursue alliances with venture companies in the Silicon Valley area to facilitate quick product development.

The statement said that around 2000, the development centre would likely develop the first products based on Matsushita's digital home concept, in which it foresees home appliances being linked to digital network services such as the Internet and digital broadcasting systems.
Morishita also said that the 64-bit game machine being developed by the company would be capable of performing various other functions apart from playing games.

The president said the company had set its own target date for the launch of the 64-bit machine, but that he could not disclose the date because the game machine was still in the process of being developed.
As for the digital video disc (DVD) market, he said DVD-ROMs will be in greater use after a standard format has largely been agreed upon.
"From September, you will see an increasing number of computers carrying DVD-ROMs, which will be in wider use in the latter half of this year," he said.
He added that he would like to focus on the U.S. market, where a full line-up of DVD software titles will be seen by this Christmas.
